I1.quote: Searched the text, tables, Fig. 5 and the experimental section for a measured amount of H2 taken up from the gas phase; not found. Every quantified H2 amount is a desorbed amount: Fig. 5 is titled "Dehydrogenation kinetics of bulk LiBH4 and nano LiBH4-ACNF" with y-axis "H2 desorbed (wt. %)", and equation 2 is "H2 desorbed (wt.%) = [(n x 2.0158)/sample weight] x 100". Rehydrogenation is described only as "the dehydrogenated sample was pressurized under 80 bar H2 (purity = 99.999%) at 350 C for 12 h", with no uptake amount or uptake curve reported; the reported 2.88 and 2.77 wt.% H2 (cycles 2 and 3) are releases on dehydrogenation.

I5.quote: New host material of activated carbon nanofiber (ACNF) prepared from carbonization and KOH activation of polyacrylonitrile (PAN)based fibers is proposed for nanocofinement of LiBH4.

notes: Paper is a primary study (LiBH4 nanoconfined in activated carbon nanofiber, ACNF); not retracted (record is_retracted false, no retraction notice in text); no duplicate-data statement. Hydrogen is stored chemically in the hydride (LiBH4 <-> LiH + B) and measured as release in a Sievert-type apparatus (main, p. 4169, Experimental: "a carefully calibrated Sievert-type apparatus"); the paper states the abstract's 11.7 and 10.1 wt.% H2 as release "with respect to LiBH4 content". Rehydrogenation uptake is never quantified, so I1 is judged not met and the code is no_conditions_stated. If a reader instead treated the cycled release as a measured uptake, I2 would fail (not_carbon): the composite is 0.0200 g ACNF with 0.0220 g LiBH4 ("52.38 wt.% of LiBH4", main p. 4172) and the sorbing phase is a hydride. Either reading makes the paper ineligible. ACNF surface area 994.5 m2/g (Table 1) is reported but was not needed for the decision.
